paragraphs.text: Glucose phosphate isomerase (GPI) deficiency is an unusual autosomal recessive cause of hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia. Paglia and Valentine (1974) reviewed hereditary GPI deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Hutton and Chilcote (1974) observed 8 children with severe hereditary nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia caused by GPI deficiency in 2 families from Kentucky and Indiana. Five of the children were living and 3 had died. All affected children were severely anemic in early life, and some needed transfusions before splenectomy. Growth and development were surprisingly normal, and no patient died of infection.
